title: Parallel quantum channel discrimination and numerical ranges in tensor product subspaces
authors: Adam Bílek, Paulina Lewandowska, Ryszard Kukulski
abstract: Quantum channel discrimination plays a crucial role in quantum information theory. Of particular interest is the case in which the channels can be discriminated perfectly. In this work, we focus on the perfect quantum channel discrimination task in a parallel scheme. We develop an SDP formulation combined with a bisection procedure to compute a quantum state for perfect discrimination in time linear in the number of copies. In addition, we obtain the minimal number of copies of quantum channels to achieve perfect discrimination. Thanks to that, we settle in the affirmative Conjecture 1 of Duan, Guo, Li and Li [arXiv:1605.02294, IEEE ISIT 2016], which characterizes the number of parallel uses needed to discriminate perfectly a distinguished family of operator subspaces. All our results are obtained using the notion and basic properties of the numerical range. In particular, the key fact that we prove and use is that the minimal angle of the numerical range of a tensor product of matrix subspaces equals the sum of the minimal angles of the numerical ranges of the individual subspaces.
summary: This work provides a comprehensive theoretical framework for analyzing perfect quantum channel discrimination in a parallel setting. It establishes that distinguishability depends on a geometric property of the operator subspace, quantified by the minimal angle of the numerical range ($	ext{sw}^*$). The paper successfully determines the minimum number of copies needed for perfect discrimination, settling a key conjecture in the field.
main_problem: The paper addresses the theoretical problem of determining the necessary and sufficient conditions for perfectly discriminating between two quantum channels ($\Phi$ and $\Psi$) when the discrimination is performed in a parallel scheme.
main_result: Perfect discrimination is possible if and only if a quantity derived from the numerical range of the associated operator subspace, $	ext{sw}^*(A) > 0$. The minimal number of copies required is $N_0 = \lceil \pi / 	ext{sw}^*(A) ceil$.
method: The authors develop an SDP formulation and heavily rely on the mathematical properties of the numerical range, particularly its behavior under tensor products, to establish the necessary conditions.
model_or_system: The system involves general quantum channels ($\Phi, \Psi$) acting on quantum states, analyzed using their Kraus operator representations and associated operator subspaces.
key_observables: The primary diagnostic tool is $	ext{sw}^*(A)$, which measures the minimal angle of the numerical range of the relevant operator subspace $A$.
important_parameters: The minimal number of copies, $N_0$, is determined by the relationship $N_0 \approx \pi / 	ext{sw}^*(A)$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the key property that the minimal angle of the numerical range of a tensor product equals the sum of the minimal angles of the individual subspaces.
paper_structure: The paper builds from defining the problem using quantum channels and the numerical range, establishing necessary and sufficient conditions via SDP, proving key properties of the numerical range under tensor products, and finally applying these results to settle a long-standing conjecture regarding the minimum number of copies.
why_interesting: The rigorous mathematical tools developed (SDP, numerical range properties) provide a powerful, general framework for analyzing distinguishability in quantum channels, which has direct implications for quantum communication protocols.
